criteria.criterion: A new integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, run with `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`, enters through the drain entry point with an interrupted Dispatched job's target/ present and asserts target/ is gone after drain start while the job's work tree and candidate remain.
criteria.evidence: The test passed (1 passed). It builds a real Dispatched job on the 'web' channel, which the drain does not work, using request_on + interrupt. It plants target/debug/big, work/main.rs and kept/<id>/work/kept.rs, then calls drain::drain with RealSteps. It asserts that target/ is gone, the work and kept files keep their bytes, Records still show the job Dispatched, the ui line 'disk       removed build directory of job <id>' appears, the lock is released and report.jobs is empty. Since no job ran, only the sweep at drain start can have removed target/.

criteria.criterion: A new test, run with `cargo test`, makes a job's lock held or its process alive (registry entry) and asserts its target/ is kept, and asserts a sweep before a later run reclaims a newly interrupted job's target/.
criteria.evidence: All three passed. The first sets up job B with a live `sleep 60` child in the registry, job C with its lock held, job E on the keep list and job D closed. All four keep target/, A loses it and every work tree stays. After the lock is released and the child is killed, B and C are reclaimed, and a newly interrupted job F is reclaimed by the next sweep. The Stub test shows one sweep at start with an empty list, then one sweep before each run. Each later list holds the job about to run and the jobs already run, and never the interrupted source 'x'. The disk.rs unit test covers the lock and the keep list on a bare StateDir.

criteria.criterion: A new test, run with `cargo test`, simulates low free disk only at the pre-producer point (via the free-bytes hook or with_free_space) and asserts the job is held as an environment stop (low disk), the status says so, and the producer is never started.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for ea539d9d3b63 (CI run 41301595930) show fmt, clippy and test all passed. I did not rerun them; I ran the five targeted tests above and all passed.

findings.summary: The sweep briefly takes the job lock of every interrupted job, so a hand-run command on that job (go, close) can fail with 'already running' during a drain.
findings.evidence: go_job (run/mod.rs:308) and close_with (manage.rs:96) bail when try_lock_job returns None. CHANGELOG and drain.rs docs state this and say a second try works. The lock is held only while target/ is removed, so the window is short; the drain's own retry locks the new job, not the source job.

findings.summary: Every sweep before a run loads the full Records from git again.
findings.evidence: reclaim_interrupted calls Records::load(&self.git, &head) on each call, and the drain calls it before every run. This is correct, since records change between runs, but it adds one records load per run.

summary:
The change passes: all seven criteria are met and there is no blocker or major finding. A drain now removes the `target/` of interrupted jobs at its start and before each run. Interrupted means the records show the job dispatched, the registry has no process for it, its lock is free and it is not one of the drain's own jobs. The lock is held while the directory is removed. It extends `sweep_idle_targets` and `remove_target` instead of building a separate mechanism. The disk is also checked just before the producer (`producer_disk_gate`); low space holds the job through `hold_for_disk`. The retry later clears that hold marker, and `athena go` on such a job says it will be read again. I ran the five new tests and all passed: the drain-start reclaim, the guards (live process, held lock, closed job, keep list, later sweep), the Stub wiring, the disk.rs unit test, and the pre-producer hold, which ends with the producer never started and a second drain retrying the job. The fmt, clippy and test results come from Athena's CI record; I did not rerun them. No toml file, `min_free_gb` default, work tree or candidate deletion is touched. Findings:
- (minor) `run/close.rs` changed but is not on the deliverables list; the change is doc only.
- (minor) While the sweep holds a job's lock, a command run by hand on that job can fail with "already running"; the change documents this.
- (nit) Each sweep loads the records again.
